editorial.titleTr: Opinion: Trump's Remarks Expose Fragility of Korea-U.S. Alliance
summaryTr: Trump calculates the Korea-U.S. alliance as a 'cost transaction,' expressing dissatisfaction with insufficient support for South Korea
Distrust between South Korea and the U.S. deepens amid issues of scaled-down joint exercises and delayed investments
The government must prove its contributions to the U.S. to secure a voice in security issues including wartime operational control and nuclear submarines
editorial.bodyTr:
President Donald Trump's recent statements are starkly revealing the fragile state of the Korea-U.S. alliance. President Trump has instructed a reduction in Korea-U.S. joint military exercises with North-U.S. dialogue in mind, and then disclosed details of a conversation with President Lee Jae-myung in which he discussed South Korea's support regarding the Strait of Hormuz, complaining that "the U.S. protects Korea with troops stationed here, but Korea does not support the U.S." While the U.S. perspective of viewing alliances as a matter of "cost and transactions" rather than values and security interests is concerning, we must reflect on whether there have been problems with our own approach that have led to the U.S. president explicitly voicing such complaints.

American media outlet Politico has labeled South Korea as the "slowest negotiator," analyzing that dissatisfaction with the pace of implementation of investments in the U.S. is behind the reduction in joint exercises. While it is unclear whether the U.S. media's reporting is accurate, it certainly reflects currents flowing through Washington. If dissatisfaction over delayed implementation of U.S. investments has resulted in an order to reduce joint exercises, that is clearly a misguided instruction. However, the South Korean government's apparent tacit approval of the reduction in joint exercises in hopes that it will help advance inter-Korean relations is also misguided. There is concern that Korea and the U.S. may be clapping hands in unison with different dreams, both going along with a matter that will inevitably have negative impacts on peninsula security.

Yesterday, President Lee Jae-myung again requested acceleration of the transfer of wartime operational control and the nuclear submarine project. However, he failed to provide answers as to why there has been no progress in the nuclear submarine project or how it will be resolved. We must not give the United States the impression that we are an ally that only receives help. Only when we demonstrate our contributions will our voice carry weight in security matters that require U.S. cooperation, such as the transition of wartime operational control or the acquisition of nuclear-powered submarines. Even if the government's desired North-U.S. dialogue materializes, if we fail to resolve the current distrust between Korea and the U.S., South Korea's space will disappear and only direct North-U.S. dealings will remain. For the government's stated role as peacemaker on the Korean Peninsula, trust in a solid Korea-U.S. alliance is essential. An alliance is not a one-way favor but a reciprocal relationship. We must be more proactive about South Korea's role, from investments in the U.S. and trade to support related to transit through the Strait of Hormuz.

editorial.title: Growing spy threat
editorial.body: Rising Chinese espionage exposes gaps in S. Korea’s counterintelligence system Two Chinese nationals were arrested earlier this month for allegedly collecting classified information related to South Korea-US military exercises and intercepting fighter jet communications near an air force base, police said on Aug. 11. One of the suspects, a Chinese man in his 40s, allegedly recruited a South Korean civilian employee at Camp Humphreys, a major US military base in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, and obtained information on the locations of US command facilities, weapons movements within the base and materials related to the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield joint military exercise. Police believe he used a military-surplus store he operated near the main gate of Camp Humphreys as a cover for his alleged espionage activities. The other suspect, a Chinese national in his 60s, was caught after setting up surveillance equipment, including a receiver and an antenna, in a hotel room near the military airport in Gunsan, North Jeolla Province, and listening in on radio communications between air traffic controllers and pilots. Police say he had repeatedly traveled to South Korea on tourist visas since 2024, eavesdropping on military communications each time the South Korean and US Air Forces held joint exercises. Both suspects were found to be former members of China's People's Liberation Army, raising suspicions that they may have been involved in an organized espionage operation. However, they cannot be charged with espionage under the Criminal Act. The reason is that while the National Assembly passed a revision in February allowing those who detect, collect, leak or transmit military secrets for foreign countries or equivalent organizations to be punished for espionage — not just for an “enemy state,” referring to North Korea — the revised law will not take effect until Sept. 13. Police charged them with aiding the enemy under the Criminal Act and violating the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act, offenses that carry lighter penalties than espionage. Suspected Chinese espionage activities targeting military intelligence in South Korea and US Forces Korea have increased in recent years. Two Chinese high school students who entered South Korea on tourist visas without a tour guide were caught photographing fighter jets taking off from and landing at Suwon Air Base in March 2025. In June 2024, Chinese students attending a university in Busan were arrested for photographing a US aircraft carrier docked in the city. Authorities found that they had illegally filmed military bases and US aircraft carriers with drones on nine occasions. In November 2024, a Chinese national was arrested after flying a drone to photograph the National Intelligence Service headquarters. According to the NIS, more than 10 cases were recorded between 2023 and 2025 in which Chinese nationals were caught secretly photographing key national facilities using drones and other equipment. The US Senate and House Armed Services Committees directed the Department of Defense to submit a report on the Chinese Communist Party’s malign activities in South Korea as part of the report accompanying the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. This can be seen as reflecting the view that China’s espionage activities in South Korea pose a threat to US defense interests. Chinese spies are targeting not only US military intelligence but also South Korea’s cutting-edge technology. In particular, South Korea’s advanced semiconductor technology is China’s most coveted industrial asset. In April, a former senior manager and a former researcher of Samsung Electronics were sentenced to prison for leaking the company's DRAM manufacturing technology and process information to CXMT, China's No. 1 DRAM maker. At a time when South Korea needs to strengthen its counterintelligence capabilities, the Lee Jae Myung administration is moving in the opposite direction. The National Intelligence Service's counterespionage investigative authority was already abolished in 2024 at the initiative of the Democratic Party of Korea, and the Lee administration, citing the alleged “insurrection” involvement as a pretext, split up and dismantled the Defense Counterintelligence Command. There are concerns about whether fragmented investigative jurisdictions can effectively thwart increasingly sophisticated espionage activities at an early stage. 지난달 11일 경찰에 따르면 한미 군사훈련 관련 기밀정보 수집 및 공군기지 인근 전투기 통신 방해 혐의로 중국인 2명이 체포됐다. 40대 중국인 용의자는 경기도 평택의 미군기지인 캠프 험프리스에 근무하는 한국인 민간인 직원을 모집해 미군 사령부 시설 위치, 기지 내 무기 이동, 을지프리덤실드 연합군사훈련 관련 자료 등의 정보를 획득한 혐의를 받고 있다. 경찰은 그가 캠프 험프리스 정문 인근에서 운영 중인 군용품점을 첩보활동의 표면조직으로 이용했을 것으로 추정하고 있다. 60대 중국인 용의자는 전북 군산의 군 비행장 인근 호텔 객실에 수신기와 안테나 등 감청 장비를 설치해 항공교통관제사와 조종사 간 무선통신을 도청한 혐의로 적발됐다. 경찰은 그가 2024년 이후 관광비자로 한국을 수차례 방문하면서 한미 공군 연합훈련이 있을 때마다 군 통신을 도청했다고 보고 있다. 두 용의자 모두 중국 인민해방군 출신으로 드러나 조직적 첩보활동과 관련됐을 가능성이 제기되고 있다. 그러나 형법상 간첩죄로 기소할 수 없다. 지난 2월 국회가 북한뿐 아니라 외국이나 이에 준하는 단체를 위해 군사기밀을 탐지, 수집, 누설, 전달하는 행위를 간첩죄로 처벌하도록 허용하는 형법 개정안을 통과시켰지만, 개정법이 9월 13일까지 시행되지 않기 때문이다. 경찰은 그들을 형법상 '적에 대한 협력' 혐의와 군사기지 및 시설 보호법 위반으로 기소했으며, 이는 간첩죄보다 낮은 형량의 범죄다. 최근 한반도 주둔 미군을 겨냥한 중국의 첩보활동이 증가하고 있다. 지난 2025년 3월 관광비자로 입국한 중국 고등학생 2명이 수원 공군기지에서 전투기 이착륙을 촬영한 혐의로 적발됐다. 2024년 6월에는 부산 소재 대학에 다니는 중국 유학생들이 부산에 정박 중인 미국 항모를 촬영한 혐의로 체포됐으며, 수사 결과 그들은 드론 등으로 군사기지와 미국 항모를 불법 촬영한 사건이 9건에 달하는 것으로 드러났다. 2024년 11월에는 국가정보원 청사를 촬영하기 위해 드론을 날린 중국인이 체포되기도 했다. 국정원에 따르면 2023년과 2025년 사이 중국인들이 드론 등 장비로 주요 국가시설을 몰래 촬영한 사건이 10건 이상 기록됐다. 미 상원 및 하원 군사위원회는 2027 회계연도 국방수권법 보고서에 포함된 내용의 일환으로 국방부에 한국에서의 중국공산당 악의적 활동에 관한 보고서 제출을 지시했다. 이는 한국에서의 중국의 첩보활동이 미국의 방위 이익에 위협이 된다는 인식을 반영하는 것으로 볼 수 있다. 중국의 스파이들은 미군 군사정보뿐 아니라 한국의 첨단기술도 겨냥하고 있다. 특히 한국의 첨단 반도체 기술은 중국이 가장 탐내하는 산업자산이다. 4월에는 삼성전자의 전직 고위 임원과 연구원이 회사의 디램 제조기술 및 공정정보를 중국 최대 디램 제조업체인 창신메모리에 유출한 혐의로 징역형을 받았다. 한국이 대공수사 역량을 강화해야 할 시점에 이준석 정부는 역방향으로 나아가고 있다. 국정원의 대공수사 수사권은 이미 2024년 민주당의 주도로 폐지됐고, 이 정부는 이른바 '반란' 개입을 구실로 국방부 대공수사대를 분리, 해체했다. 분산된 수사 관할권이 점점 정교해지는 첩보활동을 초기 단계에서 효과적으로 저지할 수 있을지에 대한 우려가 제기되고 있다.

editorials.title: Growing spy threat
editorials.body: Rising Chinese espionage exposes gaps in S. Korea’s counterintelligence system Two Chinese nationals were arrested earlier this month for allegedly collecting classified information related to South Korea-US military exercises and intercepting fighter jet communications near an air force base, police said on Aug. 11. One of the suspects, a Chinese man in his 40s, allegedly recruited a South Korean civilian employee at Camp Humphreys, a major US military base in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, and obtained information on the locations of US command facilities, weapons movements within the base and materials related to the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield joint military exercise. Police believe he used a military-surplus store he operated near the main gate of Camp Humphreys as a cover for his alleged espionage activities. The other suspect, a Chinese national in his 60s, was caught after setting up surveillance equipment, including a receiver and an antenna, in a hotel room near the military airport in Gunsan, North Jeolla Province, and listening in on radio communications between air traffic controllers and pilots. Police say he had repeatedly traveled to South Korea on tourist visas since 2024, eavesdropping on military communications each time the South Korean and US Air Forces held joint exercises. Both suspects were found to be former members of China's People's Liberation Army, raising suspicions that they may have been involved in an organized espionage operation. However, they cannot be charged with espionage under the Criminal Act. The reason is that while the National Assembly passed a revision in February allowing those who detect, collect, leak or transmit military secrets for foreign countries or equivalent organizations to be punished for espionage — not just for an “enemy state,” referring to North Korea — the revised law will not take effect until Sept. 13. Police charged them with aiding the enemy under the Criminal Act and violating the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act, offenses that carry lighter penalties than espionage. Suspected Chinese espionage activities targeting military intelligence in South Korea and US Forces Korea have increased in recent years. Two Chinese high school students who entered South Korea on tourist visas without a tour guide were caught photographing fighter jets taking off from and landing at Suwon Air Base in March 2025. In June 2024, Chinese students attending a university in Busan were arrested for photographing a US aircraft carrier docked in the city. Authorities found that they had illegally filmed military bases and US aircraft carriers with drones on nine occasions. In November 2024, a Chinese national was arrested after flying a drone to photograph the National Intelligence Service headquarters. According to the NIS, more than 10 cases were recorded between 2023 and 2025 in which Chinese nationals were caught secretly photographing key national facilities using drones and other equipment. The US Senate and House Armed Services Committees directed the Department of Defense to submit a report on the Chinese Communist Party’s malign activities in South Korea as part of the report accompanying the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. This can be seen as reflecting the view that China’s espionage activities in South Korea pose a threat to US defense interests. Chinese spies are targeting not only US military intelligence but also South Korea’s cutting-edge technology. In particular, South Korea’s advanced semiconductor technology is China’s most coveted industrial asset. In April, a former senior manager and a former researcher of Samsung Electronics were sentenced to prison for leaking the company's DRAM manufacturing technology and process information to CXMT, China's No. 1 DRAM maker. At a time when South Korea needs to strengthen its counterintelligence capabilities, the Lee Jae Myung administration is moving in the opposite direction. The National Intelligence Service's counterespionage investigative authority was already abolished in 2024 at the initiative of the Democratic Party of Korea, and the Lee administration, citing the alleged “insurrection” involvement as a pretext, split up and dismantled the Defense Counterintelligence Command. There are concerns about whether fragmented investigative jurisdictions can effectively thwart increasingly sophisticated espionage activities at an early stage. summaryTr: Youth employment has declined by 285,000 jobs over the past four years.

editorials.bodyTr: The shadow cast by artificial intelligence expansion on youth employment is becoming increasingly serious. According to the Bank of Korea, the number of jobs for young people aged 15 to 29 has declined by 285,000 over the past four years, with a striking 94 percent of these losses concentrated in sectors with high AI exposure. editorials.titleTr: Editorial: A Nation Where 6 Million Move Annually...Taxing Non-Residents as Speculators Is Problematic
summaryTr: In South Korea, where 6 million people move annually, non-resident speculation taxes are not appropriate.
Tax policies that overlook the reality of frequent housing transfers become a burden on ordinary citizens.
Designing tax systems based on the oversimplified equation of non-resident equals speculator creates significant side effects.
